items.followUp: What is meant by data storage?

rubric.why: Identifies that storage capacity refers to how much data can be stored.
rubric.description: States that a storage device can hold more data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for expressing the ability to store a larger amount of data.

rubric.why: Connects the idea to the capacity of storage devices.
rubric.description: Explains that the device’s capacity is increasing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to increasing storage capacity or a storage device holding more information.

modelAnswer: Increasing storage capacity means that a storage device can hold a larger amount of data.
As technology improves, devices can store more information than before.

items.followUp: What is the role of a router in sending data across the Internet?

rubric.why: Describes the basic function of routing as selecting or forwarding data along a route.
rubric.description: States that routing selects or forwards a path for data packets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning selection of a route/path or forwarding packets.

rubric.why: Shows that routing moves packets through the network toward their intended endpoint.
rubric.description: Mentions routers directing packets from source to destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying routers and the source-to-destination journey.

modelAnswer: Routing is the process of choosing a path for data packets to travel across the Internet.
Routers forward the packets from the source toward their destination.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and describe any two of its characteristics.

rubric.why: Identifies a flowchart as a visual representation.
rubric.description: Defines a flowchart as a graphical or diagrammatic representation of a process or algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a diagram/graphical representation of steps or an algorithm.

rubric.why: Recognises the terminal symbol and its function.
rubric.description: Gives the terminal symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the oval/terminal symbol as start or end.

rubric.why: Recognises a standard symbol used to show processing.
rubric.description: Gives the process symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a rectangle as a processing step or instruction.

rubric.why: Recognises a standard symbol used for input or output.
rubric.description: Gives the input/output symbol and its use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a parallelogram as input or output.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of the steps of an algorithm or process using standard symbols.
An oval (terminal) symbol shows the start or end of a flowchart.
A rectangle (process) symbol shows a processing step or instruction.
A parallelogram symbol shows input or output.

items.followUp: Name any four layers of the OSI model and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the function of the Physical layer.
rubric.description: Defines the Physical layer by its transmission of raw bits or signals over a medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Physical-layer function.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the Data Link layer’s role in communication between directly connected devices.
rubric.description: Defines the Data Link layer by framing or link-level delivery/error control.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Data Link-layer function.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the Network layer’s role in addressing and routing.
rubric.description: Defines the Network layer by logical addressing or routing packets between networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Network-layer function.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of the Transport layer’s role in end-to-end delivery.
rubric.description: Defines the Transport layer by end-to-end delivery, segmentation, or reliable transfer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct Transport-layer function.

modelAnswer: The Physical layer transmits raw bits as signals over the communication medium.
The Data Link layer organizes data into frames and manages communication over a link.
The Network layer uses logical addresses and routes packets between networks.
The Transport layer provides end-to-end delivery of data between devices.

items.followUp: Explain the Caesar cipher and give one example of its use.

rubric.why: States the central idea of substitution ciphers.
rubric.description: Explains that plaintext letters or characters are replaced with other letters or characters.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing replacement according to a cipher rule or key.

rubric.why: Identifies the Caesar method and its fixed-shift rule.
rubric.description: Describes Caesar cipher as shifting letters by a fixed number of positions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the method or correctly describing its shift.

rubric.why: Identifies a simple substitution method in which each letter has a fixed substitute.
rubric.description: Describes monoalphabetic substitution as using one fixed substitution alphabet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or correctly describing monoalphabetic substitution.

rubric.why: Identifies a method that uses more than one substitution alphabet.
rubric.description: Describes polyalphabetic substitution as using multiple substitution alphabets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or correctly describing polyalphabetic substitution.

modelAnswer: A substitution cipher is an encryption method in which plaintext letters are replaced by other letters or symbols according to a key.
In a Caesar cipher, each letter is shifted by a fixed number of places in the alphabet.
A monoalphabetic cipher uses one fixed substitution alphabet, so each plaintext letter has a fixed substitute.
A polyalphabetic cipher uses more than one substitution alphabet to encrypt the message.

items.followUp: Write any two steps used to solve a problem.

rubric.why: Recognises the initial step of clarifying what the problem asks.
rubric.description: Names understanding or defining the problem as a problem-solving step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid step such as understanding or defining the problem.

rubric.why: Recognises another valid step in the problem-solving process.
rubric.description: Names any other valid problem-solving step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct valid step, such as designing an algorithm, implementing, testing, or evaluating the solution.

modelAnswer: Understand and define the problem clearly.
Design an algorithm or plan to solve the problem.

items.followUp: What is meant by the time complexity of an algorithm?

rubric.why: Shows that efficiency concerns how well an algorithm performs.
rubric.description: States that algorithm efficiency measures how effectively an algorithm solves a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting efficiency with an algorithm’s performance or resource use.

rubric.why: Identifies the resources used to assess efficiency.
rubric.description: Mentions the time and/or memory/resources required by the algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming time, memory/space, or computational resources.

modelAnswer: The efficiency of an algorithm is how effectively it solves a problem using computational resources.
It is commonly judged by the time it takes and the memory it requires.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the process symbol in a flowchart?

rubric.why: Checks that the student knows the terminal symbol marks the beginning.
rubric.description: States that a terminal symbol indicates the start of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the start/beginning.

rubric.why: Checks that the student knows the terminal symbol marks completion.
rubric.description: States that a terminal symbol indicates the end of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the end/stop/termination.

modelAnswer: The terminal symbol is used to show the beginning of a flowchart.
It is also used to show where the flowchart ends.
